Rashi on Gittin 69a:10:2.english: Sliced beets - Trimming of beets, [in Old French:] mencendure [mincing]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:10:3.hebrew: פרידא - מין עשב, וי"א מדיירישר"ש:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:10:3.english: Perida - A type of herb, and some say merisiers [wild cherries]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:10:4.english: And a corresponding [amount] - [Equal to] the measure of all of these:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:10:5.english: Kanta petirta - Entrailles [Old French for entrails] of an animal that was the firstborn of its mother's womb:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:1.english: For kakha - [This is] an illness of the inner teeth:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:2.english: A single garlic - A head of garlic that has only one clove:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:3.english: And grind it - He should crush it:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:4.english: On the thumbnail [atufra de'alyona] - On the nail of the thumb of the hand:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:5.english: And he should be careful with his flesh - [meaning] that that garlic should not touch his flesh:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:11:6.english: Because it is harmful [causing] whiteness - Leprosy:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:1.hebrew: לחינכי - אבעבועות הגדילים בגרון כמין גלנט, ובלשון רומי אשטרנגיילו"ן:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:1.english: For *chinchei* - Swellings that grow in the throat like a *gland* [acorn-like swelling], and in the Roman language [Old French]: *estranguillon* [quinsy]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:11.english: And chumarta dikhshuta - the flower of the hop [plant], [called] homlon [in Old French]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:12.english: Like a nut - The measure of a nut:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:2.hebrew: חומתי כי ממרו - עלי של חומם, פילטרו, טוב לרפואה זו כמין עשב שקורין ממרו בלשון ארמי:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:2.english: Chomti is like mamru - The leaf of chomem [Spanish chamomile], pelitro [pellitory], is good for this remedy, like a type of herb that is called mamru in Aramaic:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:3.english: And the root of chomti - The root of the chimum [plant, i.e.,] pellitory [piletro]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:4.hebrew: עדיף - לרפואה מממרו. ממרו — שבדמוני', לשון מורי:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:4.english: Is preferable - for healing over mamru. Mamru [is] shavdemoni — [this is] the wording of my teacher:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:6.hebrew: לאוקומי - החולי, שלא ינפח יותר מדאי:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:6.english: To stabilize - [meaning, to hold] the illness, so that it does not swell too much:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:7.hebrew: לבשולי - האבעבועות, שתקבץ לחה שלהן לתוכן, שתהא יוצאה כשיבקעו אותו:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:7.english: To ripen - the abscesses, so that their fluid gathers inside them, so that it will come out when they break it open:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:8.english: Bran at the top of the sifter - Coarse bran that floats to the top in the sifter when sifting:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:12:9.english: And lentils in their dirt - Lentils with [the] dirt in which they were uprooted:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:1.hebrew: לפתוחי - האבעבועות של אשטרנגיילו"ן, שיבקעו ותצא הליחה:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:1.english: To open - the blisters of estranguillon [quinsy], so that they burst and the pus comes out:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:2.english: Let [his friend] blow for him - into his throat:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:3.hebrew: בגילא דחיטתא - שהוא חלול, ויכניס זרע השחלים לתוכו בראשו אחד, ויכניסנו בתוך פיו של חולה עד הבליעה, וינפח חבירו בראש האחר, ויצאו השחלים ויפלו ויחנו על החולי:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:3.english: With a straw of wheat - for it is hollow, and one inserts the cress seed into it at one end, and inserts it into the sick person's mouth up to [the point of] swallowing, and his friend blows into the other end, and the cress [seeds] will come out, fall, and settle upon the affliction:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:4.english: To heal - [meaning] to grow new flesh, to heal the rupture:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:13:5.english: From the shade of the bathroom - From beneath the shade of stones arranged for a latrine in the fields and fashioned like a seat:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:1.hebrew: לברסם - חולי שקורין צוריי"ר, והוא בא מן הראש דרך החוטם:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:1.english: For barsam - [this is] an illness that they call tzoreir [catarrh], and it comes from the head through the nose:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:2.hebrew: כי פיסתקא דנשדור - כשיעור גלנט של ארז, מסם נשדור שקורין אמוניקא:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:2.english: Like a pistaka of nishdor - The measure of a cedar nut [gland], of the substance nishdor, which is called amoniaka [sal ammoniac]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:3.english: Sweet galbanum - sweet galbanum [ḥelvenah], which is called galma [galbanum]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:5.english: Natla - a vessel holding a quarter-[log]:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:6.english: Clear wine - Fine, clear wine that is not red:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:7.hebrew: וכי בשיל נשדור בשיל כוליה - זה סימן יהיה לך: לכשיבשל הנשדור, בידוע ששאר סמנין מבושלין, לפי שהוא קשה:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:14:7.english: And once nishdor [ammonia] is cooked, all of it is cooked - This shall be a sign for you: when the nishdor is cooked, it is certain that the other ingredients are cooked, because it is hard:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:1.english: For beroketi - An illness of the eye that is called teila [a film/cataract].

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:2.english: Of seven colors - spotted with seven colors due to old age:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:3.english: And dry it in the shade - that is to say, not [dried] by the sun:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:4.english: Two portions of stibium and one portion of it - two parts kohl [stibium] and one part of it:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:5.hebrew: תלתא מכחלי - מכחול הוא כנף עוף או כף רחב דק של עץ, שנוטל בו הכחול ונותן בעין:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:5.english: Three eyebrushes - A makhul [eyebrush] is a bird's wing [feather] or a thin, wide wooden spoon, with which one takes the eye-paint [stibium] and places [it] in the eye:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:7.english: Let him fill - He should place [it] in his eye:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:8.hebrew: דאי לא - מיזדהר דלא לימלי טפי, פקע עיניה:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:1:8.english: For if not - [meaning, if he does not] take care not to put in more, his eye will burst:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:1.english: For night blindness - blindness that comes upon a person at night:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:10.english: He should untie - he should untie the knot from his leg:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:11.english: In the bavita of its eye - In the pupil of its eye:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:2.english: Shudra barka - a rope of animal hair and of the tail of a horse and a cow:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:3.english: And he should tie one of his legs and one leg of a dog - He should tie one of his legs and the dog's leg to the two ends of the rope:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:4.english: And let children rattle pottery shards behind him - Children should rattle broken pieces of earthenware behind him:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:5.english: And they shall say - this incantation:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:6.hebrew: אסא כלבא אכסא תרנגול - זקן כלב, שוטה תרנגול:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:6.english: Asa kalba achsa tarnegol - Old [is the] dog, foolish [is the] rooster:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:2:8.english: And let them place them for him - [That is,] the residents of the houses [should place] those pieces of raw meat in the socket of the door:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:3:2.english: On the shard of a bloodletter - A repulsive earthenware vessel into which they let blood:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:3:3.hebrew: ונימא ליה עוירא - לפתיחא, "הב לי ואיכול":
Rashi on Gittin 69a:3:3.english: And let the blind man say to him - [meaning] to the seeing man: "Give me [something] to eat."

Rashi on Gittin 69a:4:1.english: Pappi Sheila, etc. - It is an incantation.

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:1.english: Taste from a bucket in silver water - It is an incantation:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:2.english: Ashla depurya - A rope of a bed:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:5.english: And the red [portion] of a palm branch - Something red that grows on a palm branch.

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:6.hebrew: ונגדיל פתילתא - לשון גדילים, יעשה פתילה מן הצמר:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:6.english: And spin strings - [This is] an expression [related to] "braids" [gedilim]; he should make a string from the wool:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:7.english: And let him soak [them] in vinegar - He should soak [them] in vinegar:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:8.hebrew: וניגדביל - יגלגלנו באפר, וידבק האפר בו:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:5:8.english: And let him roll - He shall roll it in the ash, and the ash will adhere to it:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:7:1.english: And let them pour on him - via the gutter:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:8:1.english: Sticks - the straw adheres to the blood:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:9:1.hebrew: כיון - דדמא דכבדא, שהיא תלויה למטה מן הריאה, עולה למעלה ונפיק דרך הפה:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:9:1.english: Since [it comes from his mouth] - [this is because] the blood of the liver, which hangs below the lung, rises upward and exits through the mouth:

Rashi on Gittin 69a:9:2.hebrew: אימר אתמוחי אתמח - כולה כבדא, ולא נשתייר הימנה כלום, ונפל לריאה דרך קנה הכבד שמחובר לקנה של ריאה:
Rashi on Gittin 69a:9:2.english: Say that [it] has dissolved - [meaning] the entire liver, and nothing of it remained, and it fell into the lung through the tube of the liver, which is connected to the tube of the lung:

Tosafot on Gittin 69a:11:1.hebrew: לככא - שינים כדפי' בקונטרס כאן, ולא כמו שפירש בעלמא (ע"ז דף כח:) דהיינו חניכיים, מדאמרינן בערבי פסחים (דף קיג.): לא תעקר ככא; וכן בחולין (דף נט:): נתור ככי ושיני דגברי — וזה לא שייך לומר בחניכיים:
Tosafot on Gittin 69a:11:1.english: For kaka - [This means] teeth, as Rashi explained here, and not as he explained elsewhere (Avodah Zarah 28b) that it means gums, since we say in [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (113a): "Do not extract a tooth [kaka]," and likewise in Chullin (59b): "The molars [kakei] and teeth of men fall out" — and this cannot be said regarding gums:

Tosafot on Gittin 69a:1:1.hebrew: לברוקתי - הכא משמע דיש לה רפואה, וכן בפ' המוציא יין (שבת דף עח.) נמי קאמר: שכן כוחלין לברוקתי. וקשה, דבבכורות (דף לח:) חשיב ליה גבי מומין הקבועין! ואומר רבינו יצחק, דכל מה שאינו עובר מאיליו או ע"י רפואה קלה, חשיב מום קבוע. אי נמי, רפואה דהכא ודהמוציא היינו בתחילת החולי, אבל בסוף החולי אין לו רפואה:
Tosafot on Gittin 69a:1:1.english: For eye disease [beroketi] - Here it is implied that it has a cure, and similarly in the chapter [entitled] Hamotzi Yayin (Shabbat 78a) [the Gemara] also says: "For so they apply eye-paint for beroketi." And this is difficult, for in Bekhorot (38b) [the Mishnah] counts it among permanent blemishes! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that anything that does not pass on its own or through a mild remedy is considered a permanent blemish. Alternatively, the cure [mentioned] here and in Hamotzi [Yayin] is at the beginning of the illness, whereas at the end of the illness it has no cure:
